trials.name: BioFINDER - Primary Care
trials.population: Patients seeking medical care due to mild cognitive symptoms in primary care units.
trials.primary_endpoint: Presence of brain AD pathology as determined by CSF AD biomarkers
trials.results_summary: The published JAMA 2024 readout showed the APS2 algorithm (combining p-tau217 ratio and Abeta42/40 ratio) had 88-92% diagnostic accuracy in the primary care cohort, significantly outperforming standard clinical evaluation.

trials.name: BioFINDER 2
trials.population: Healthy individuals, SCD/MCI, AD dementia, and other dementias evaluated in memory clinics (secondary care).
trials.primary_endpoint: Clinical diagnosis according to consensus group decision blinded to the diagnostic test
trials.results_summary: The JAMA 2024 readout demonstrated that APS2 testing had around 91% diagnostic accuracy in the secondary care cohort, significantly outperforming standard evaluation by dementia specialists.

trials.name: HT-4253-APOE-002
trials.population: APOE4 carriers aged 50-75 with a positive PrecivityAD2 APS2 score (high risk).
trials.primary_endpoint: Proportion of participants demonstrating improvement in amyloid risk profile (transitioning to lower APS2 score)

trials.name: BBM-01-2025
trials.population: Patients referred to the MoCA Clinic with cognitive impairment or complaints.
trials.primary_endpoint: Time to diagnosis (eligible vs not eligible for anti-amyloid medication)

trials.name: ADELAIDE
trials.population: Patients presenting with symptoms of mild cognitive impairment with suspected AD pathology.
trials.primary_endpoint: Time to achieve >=90% Diagnostic Confidence for AD or Non-AD

related_evidence.description: JAMA publication of the BioFINDER primary and secondary care cohorts demonstrating superior diagnostic accuracy of APS2 and %p-tau217.
C2N Diagnostics submits PrecivityAD2 blood test for US FDA regulatory approval.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence supporting the use of the APS2 blood biomarker (and p-tau217 percentage) for Alzheimer's diagnosis is exceptionally strong, driven largely by the robust, prospective Swedish BioFINDER cohorts. The BioFINDER-Primary Care (NCT06120361) and BioFINDER 2 (NCT03174938) studies successfully demonstrated that these blood tests achieve approximately 90% diagnostic accuracy, drastically outperforming standard evaluations by both primary care physicians and dementia specialists. The widespread acceptance of this test is further evidenced by its integration as a screening and efficacy endpoint in therapeutic trials (e.g., NCT07399171 for Halia Therapeutics) and diagnostic workflow trials (NCT07041450). While C2N Diagnostics withdrew its own US health-services study (ADELAIDE; NCT06856681) prior to enrollment, they have submitted the PrecivityAD2 test for FDA approval. Collectively, the high positive and negative predictive values reported in multiple care settings solidify APS2 as a practice-changing diagnostic tool.
